history.summary: PROVISIONAL IDENTIFICATION — no shrine named exactly 'Shakti Mandir' is documented in Koderma town or district; this row is mapped to the district's only documented major Shakti shrine, the Shaktipeeth of Maa Chanchala Devi, with the name mismatch flagged. It stands about 400 ft up a hill roughly 33 km from the district headquarters on the Koderma-Giridih highway and is regarded as one of the forms of Goddess Durga. A nearby cave on the hill has rock paintings of four forms of Durga, but entry is difficult through a narrow passage. Large numbers of devotees visit on Tuesdays and Saturdays; the prasad is arwa rice and mishri, use of sindoor (vermilion) is prohibited, and devotees must bathe before entering (local belief holds violations bring insect bites). Many marriages and mundan ceremonies are solemnized here. Coordinates are approximate (Jainagar-block area on the Koderma-Giridih highway) — no exact published coordinates found. If the CSV intended a smaller 'Shiv Shakti Mandir' in Jhumri Telaiya or another local shrine, this record should be corrected.

name: Shaktipeeth Maa Chanchala Devi
town_description: Koderma (also spelled Kodarma) is the administrative headquarters of Koderma district in northern Jharkhand, on the northern end of the Chota Nagpur plateau. Once famous as the 'mica capital' of India, the district's mica industry declined and many units closed; the larger commercial city nearby is Jhumri Telaiya. The district's notable Devi shrine is the Shaktipeeth of Maa Chanchala Devi on the Koderma-Giridih highway.
